title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
abstract: Studies document evidence attribution without requiring models to directly emit coordinates. Models quote supporting text and a multimodal retriever maps those quotations back to page regions, providing an alternative route from answer evidence to precise source location.

title: VersionRAG: Version-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Evolving Documents
abstract: Presents a version-aware RAG framework that models document evolution with a hierarchical graph containing version sequences, content boundaries, and changes between document states. Retrieval routes version-sensitive questions through version filtering and change-tracking paths.

title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning
abstract: Models long-document VQA as evidence-graph reasoning. The framework performs evidence localization, structured document parsing, and explicit graph construction with node-level provenance so evidence composition across multiple pages can be inspected.

title: A model for multimodal reference resolution
abstract: Provides an early formal model for resolving natural-language names and pronouns against graphical objects in a multimodal message, explicitly treating the antecedent as potentially residing in a graphical rather than linguistic context.

title: Disambiguating Reference in Visually Grounded Dialogues through Joint Modeling of Textual and Multimodal Semantic Structures
abstract: Unifies textual reference resolution and grounding to visual objects in dialogue, with particular attention to ambiguous pronouns and ellipses. This is transfer evidence for references in communication text that point into an associated visual artifact.

title: M3Grounder: Mask-Based Multi-Span and Multi-Granular Grounding for Document QA
abstract: Links individual generated answer spans to pixel-level evidence masks in document images. It also represents evidence at nested phrase, line, and block granularities and evaluates multi-span grounding on complex document layouts.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Multimomal Generation for Document Question Answering
abstract: Introduces MMDocRAG for long multimodal documents containing text, images, and tables. Its questions include multi-page cross-modal evidence chains and its evaluation explicitly measures multimodal evidence selection and integration.

title: DLaVA: Document Language and Vision Assistant for Answer Localization with Enhanced Interpretability and Trustworthiness
abstract: Adds answer-localization capabilities to multimodal models for Document VQA so answers can be spatially traced back to their source locations rather than evaluated only for textual correctness.

title: Unambiguous Scene Text Segmentation With Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Introduces language-conditioned segmentation of specific scene-text instances. Referring expressions are mapped to pixel-level text regions, providing transfer evidence for grounding language to precise text-rich image regions.

title: Transformer-based dynamic cell bounding box refinement for end-to-end Table Structure Recognition
abstract: Adds a coordinate decoder that iteratively refines individual cell bounding boxes while jointly modeling table structure. The method is particularly relevant when cell-level provenance must survive table extraction.

title: GRAVL-BERT: Graphical Visual-Linguistic Representations for Multimodal Coreference Resolution
abstract: Resolves cross-modal coreferences in multi-turn dialogue by jointly modeling scene objects, visual relationships, dialogue history, and metadata. It is transfer evidence for resolving message expressions against attached visual content.

title: Not All References Resolve Alike: Fine-Grained Assessment of Complementary Cross-modal Reference Resolution
abstract: Studies cross-modal reference resolution at a fine-grained level, examining how meanings expressed in one modality are associated with entities or events expressed in another. It is transfer evidence rather than a workplace-document benchmark.

title: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
abstract: Evaluates agents on professional spreadsheet generation, debugging, and visualization workflows involving complex workbooks. Tasks average many worksheets and require coordinated modifications and cross-sheet dependencies rather than isolated table operations.

title: General Table Question Answering via Answer-Formula Joint Generation
abstract: Treats spreadsheet formulas as logical forms for complex table question answering and jointly generates an answer and its formula. It provides evidence about formula-based reasoning but does not by itself establish full workbook-level understanding.

title: Scene-Text Oriented Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Defines a referring-expression task in which linguistic descriptions can refer to text visible inside an image. Its model explicitly aligns scene-text semantics, visual regions, and referring expressions, making it a close transfer analogue for references such as labels or highlighted content in screenshots.

title: Heterogeneous Element-Aware Cross-Version Differencing of Scientific Documents via Layout-Aware Alignment and Structure-Aware Reasoning
abstract: Proposes a layout-aware cross-version differencing framework that decomposes scientific PDFs into typed text, table, formula, and figure elements, aligns corresponding elements using spatial, content, and structural compatibility, and localizes semantic changes between document revisions.

title: Semi-supervised multimodal coreference resolution in image narrations
abstract: Studies coreference resolution and fine-grained narrative grounding when a longer text is paired with an image. The setting is a transfer analogue for resolving expressions in a message against associated visual evidence.

title: SentryLine: Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Evolving Documents in Oncology Care
abstract: Describes evidence-grounded QA over living oncology guidelines. The system returns inline citations, temporal verification, and drift information when guideline documents have changed across versions.

title: Towards Robust Real-World Spreadsheet Understanding with Multi-Agent Multi-Format Reasoning
abstract: Presents SpreadsheetAgent, which incrementally inspects spreadsheet regions through code results, rendered images, and LaTeX tables. It first constructs structural sketches and row or column summaries and then verifies relevant regions during downstream reasoning.

title: SpreadsheetBench: Towards Challenging Real World Spreadsheet Manipulation
abstract: Introduces a benchmark built from real spreadsheet-user requests and heterogeneous spreadsheet files containing multiple tables, non-standard structures, and non-textual elements. It evaluates end-to-end spreadsheet manipulation rather than normalized-table QA alone.

title: Where is this coming from? Making groundedness count in the evaluation of Document VQA models
abstract: Proposes Document VQA evaluation metrics that account for both semantic correctness and multimodal placement of an answer in its source document. Human evaluation is used to validate whether the grounded scoring better distinguishes supported from poorly grounded predictions.

title: MM-Doc-R1: Training Agents for Long Document Visual Question Answering through Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Uses a vision-aware multi-turn agent to iteratively find and synthesize information in long documents. It is relevant to cross-page evidence discovery although its main contribution is agent training rather than a complete fine-grained provenance hierarchy.

title: TRH2TQA: Table Recognition with Hierarchical Relationships to Table Question-Answering on Business Table Images
abstract: Extracts business-table images into structured representations that preserve merged cells and parent-child header relationships before performing table QA. The work directly targets hierarchical table structure needed to interpret complex financial documents.

title: Look as You Think: Unifying Reasoning and Visual Evidence Attribution for Verifiable Document RAG via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Introduces a Chain-of-Evidence representation that attaches reasoning references to document regions using bounding boxes and page indexes. The reinforcement-learning method trains models to generate answers together with progressively attributable visual evidence.

title: DocLLM: A layout-aware generative language model for multimodal document understanding
abstract: Represents enterprise-document text together with bounding-box layout information and models cross-alignment between semantic and spatial modalities. It targets irregular layouts and heterogeneous business documents such as forms, invoices, reports, and contracts.
